My other apps

The ones people download most, and a few I'm proudest of.

CallShield · Android · ⭐81 · 4,000+ downloads
Blocks spam calls and flags spam texts with an on-device model and a signed database of 51,000+ numbers. No API keys and no subscription.

OpenLumen · Android · ⭐19 · 1,400+ downloads
A screen color filter that changes the display itself instead of painting a layer on top. Warm the screen on a schedule or fix a panel's color cast, fully offline.

SwiftFloris · Android · ⭐38 · 1,300+ downloads
A SwiftKey-style keyboard built on FlorisBoard, with no internet permission at all. Import your SwiftKey or Gboard dictionary and it all stays on your phone.

Rclone Browser NG · Windows, macOS, Linux · ⭐20
A desktop app for rclone that picks up where the abandoned RcloneBrowser left off. Browse any remote, encrypted ones included, while transfers run in the background.

AppManagerNG · Android · ⭐201 · 13,000+ downloads
See every app on your phone and what it can reach. Freeze or remove the bloat and back up the rest, with or without root.

SnapCrop · Android · ⭐14
Catches each screenshot as you take it and opens it in an editor with the status and nav bars already cropped off. Scrolling capture and automatic redaction of sensitive text are free.

HushFacebook Web · Browser · ⭐47 · 3,000+ downloads
Takes ads and suggested posts out of Facebook in a desktop browser, and adds downloads and privacy switches. Runs as a userscript or a Chrome extension.

ZeusWatch · Android · ⭐15 · 1,300+ downloads
Weather with a second opinion. Put forecast providers side by side to see where the models disagree, then keep the sources you trust. No account needed.

AlarmClockXtreme · Android · ⭐50 · 2,000+ downloads
An alarm clock for heavy sleepers. Exact scheduling and 30 dismiss challenges get you up and keep you up, with no ads and no account.

OpenTasker · Android · ⭐213 · 14,000+ downloads
Phone automation in the spirit of Tasker, fully open source. Rules you can read at a glance and 78 built-in actions, all running on your phone.

OpenNetLimit · Windows · ⭐28 · 1,100+ downloads
See which apps are using your connection, then cap the ones that hog it. Per-app limits, traffic history, quotas and schedules on Windows.

eddyizm.com

Creating a new personal site, blog using django and python.

Set up

This guide assumes you already have python 3 and git installed.

Clone repository

git clone https://github.com/eddyizm/eddyizm.git

Create a virtual environment

python -m venv </path/to/new/virtual/environment>

Changed directory and activate virtual environment

   cd </path/to/new/virtual/environment>  
   Scripts\activate
   # in bash use this instead
   source Scripts/activate
   cd </pathToGitProject>

Install Django and verify version installed

pip install django   
django-admin --version

How this card is built
  • The card is an SVG (dark_mode.svg) generated by the local gsy_profilecard package. Dark mode only (ASCII avatars look poor on a white background).
  • The ASCII avatar on the left is baked once by tools/make_art.py from the source portrait (tools/avatar.png) into art.json.
  • Right-hand text comes from profile.toml — edit that file to change any copy without touching code.
  • GitHub stats (repos / stars / followers / commits / LOC) are refreshed daily at 04:17 UTC by .github/workflows/update.yml, which commits the new SVG back to the repo.

Local usage:

make install   # pip install -e ".[dev]"
make update    # regenerate dark_mode.svg; needs ACCESS_TOKEN in env or env.txt
make test      # pytest

ACCESS_TOKEN only needs read:user + public_repo scopes.

Credit: this card is inspired by and adapted from glrodasz/glrodasz — huge thanks to @glrodasz for the original Neofetch-style profile card idea.
